detailed_description:
The target uses realistic cinematic photography with restrained handheld movement, natural indoor lighting, accurate Mandarin lip synchronization, and dry situational comedy. The entire video remains in the first-person viewpoint of one unseen person standing outside and then entering the room. No part of the camera operator’s face or body is visible except one hand pushing the door. Total duration is exactly 15 seconds.

The room contains two fixed gaming desks placed side by side. <Subject 1> always occupies the left station and <Subject 2> always occupies the right station. Each station has one monitor, one keyboard, one mouse, and one headset. Their equipment, chairs, hand positions, and seating order never swap or duplicate. Both monitors display the same ongoing CS2-style tactical first-person shooter match from two different player perspectives. The game has realistic rifles, a clean competitive HUD, a sunlit urban combat map, team indicators, muzzle flashes, and tactical movement, but no unrelated game genres or third-person gameplay.

[Shot 1] The video begins outside a closed bedroom door. A first-person right hand reaches into frame, turns the handle, and pushes the door inward. The camera walks into the room in one continuous take. Through the widening doorway, <Subject 1> and <Subject 2> are revealed sitting Her outfit follows the reference image. Fast mouse movements and keyboard taps show that both are actively playing.

At 00:01.700, the first-person camera advances slowly behind the two chairs. On the left monitor, <Subject 1>’s character watches a long outdoor corridor where several opponents appear. <Subject 1> (S1) tightens her grip on the mouse and shouts urgently into her headset, <d>[Chinese] A大！A大！A大一万人！</d> Her head stays directed toward her monitor while her left hand continues operating the keyboard.

At 00:04.300, <Subject 2>’s right monitor shows her character rushing toward the same combat area. <Subject 2> (S2) leans closer, rapidly taps the keyboard, and answers with determination, <d>[Chinese] 来了，我上了！</d> Gunfire intensifies on both screens. A moment later, her character pushes forward alone while <Subject 1>’s character turns and retreats. <Subject 2> freezes for half a beat, looks toward <Subject 1> without removing her hands from the controls, and complains, <d>[Chinese] 哎？我上了，你咋跑了？</d>

At 00:09.000, <Subject 1> keeps retreating on the left monitor. She gives a guilty sideways smile, slightly hunches her shoulders, and replies playfully, <d>[Chinese] 我保把枪，嘿嘿。</d> She continues controlling the same character with the same keyboard and mouse.

At 00:11.100, the first-person camera stops directly behind and between their chairs. The unseen visitor (S3), speaking from the camera position in a confused, mildly exasperated voice, asks, <d>[Chinese] 不是说回家看我工作流的吗？</d> Both women pause for a fraction of a second and slowly turn their heads halfway toward the camera while keeping their hands on their controls. End at exactly 00:15.000 on their awkward, caught-in-the-act expressions.

Only natural diegetic sound is present: the door handle turning, door hinges, soft footsteps, computer fans, rapid keyboard tapping, mouse clicks, chair creaks, headset dialogue, and synchronized tactical-game audio from the two monitors. Game sounds include directional footsteps, short rifle bursts, ricochets, reload clicks, distant grenade impacts, and brief radio effects. Dialogue remains clear and foregrounded.

N/A — no background music, score, melody, or musical sound effects.
